turns.text: Still. No tail-flick, no shifting weight, nothing a camera could flag as motion worth logging. Three crates back from the guarded stack, downwind, where tuna-scent sits so thick it registers behind the teeth instead of in the nose — and under it, older, a rust-brown smear along one crate's corner that reads as old blood before it reads as anything else.

the loading dock stacks eight crates high under a floodlight buzzing one flicker short of dead, NEKOCORP TUNA — PREMIUM RESERVE stenciled fresh over older stencils scrubbed but not gone. two sentry drones hover at each end of the row, rotors idling low, and a third unit — boxier, unhurried — trundles the gap between them on treads, its speaker crackling through a warm-up hiss like something about to be announced.

Ears pin flat at the rotor-idle pitch before the hiss even resolves into words — old reflex, older than any one drone. Whatever's coming through that speaker next, the body already knows to brace for it the way it braces for weather.

the treaded unit finds its voice: BOUNTY ADVISORY — SECTOR NINE. SUBJECT: KNIFEBOY. FORTY THOUSAND LOYALTY POINTS. CHARGES: SUPPLY CHAIN INTERFERENCE, UNAUTHORIZED NOTE-LEAVING, REPEATED THEFT OF PREMIUM RESERVE STOCK. points expire before capture and cannot be combined with other promotional offers. the message loops once, then again, indifferent to who might be close enough to hear it.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

Hearing your own name come back at you through a speaker built to sell milk is not the same as fear — closer to an itch, personal now in a way the rust-brown smear on the crate corner already was. Moves closer instead of off, paw finding the next patch of shadow between floodlight sweeps.

the sentries tighten their spacing half a meter, floodlight sweep quickening by a fraction nobody not already watching for it would notice. up on the gantry rail above the dock, something crouches at the very edge of the light's reach — a shape wearing two black discs where eyes should throw shine back, watching the whole row without once being caught in a beam. it isn't here for the bounty. it's just here, the way it's always somewhere, cataloguing.

One glance up, one nod's worth of stillness held a half-second longer than it needs to be — recognition, not alarm, the kind that passes between crews who've never once had reason to cross each other. Eyes drop back to the crates. Whatever the gantry logs tonight isn't this cat's problem to guess at.

the treaded unit completes its sweep and idles at the row's far end, cycling down between broadcasts. one crate seam, second from the top, shows a hairline gap where the last forklift set it down a finger's width off true — enough for a determined mouth to work at, not enough for the drones' pattern-recognition to flag as anything but normal wear.

Up the stack in three moves, claws finding purchase on stencil-rough cardboard, weight distributed low the whole climb. Teeth find the seam's gap first, testing it before committing — old habit, the kind that's kept teeth intact through worse crates than this one.

the seam gives with a soft cardboard groan, packing ice sliding cold against a nose already committed to the gap — inside, foil pouches stacked tight, PREMIUM RESERVE stamped on each one, cold enough to sting, real enough that the smell alone could carry three blocks on a still night.

One pouch worked loose and gripped tight in the jaw, and before the retreat starts, a paw finds the ash-dust settled along the crate's underside from some old floodlight burnout — presses it once into the cardboard, drags it into a shape that isn't for reading, only for whoever finds this crate next to recognize the same way a scent-mark gets recognized. Down the stack faster than the climb up.

the treaded unit's cycle resets a half-second after the shape lands on the cardboard, floodlight sweeping back across the row and finding nothing but crates stacked exactly where its own log says they should be — the gap already too small to register, the ash-mark below its sensors' notice entirely. the gantry shape is gone from the rail, gone the way it's always gone, no trace of when.

Off the stack, off the dock, low and fast through the gap between two idling forklifts, pouch gripped tight enough to mute the cold leaking through foil. The rust-brown smear on that one crate corner stays behind, unremarked on, unexplained — some other night's question, not tonight's.

past the forklifts, the dock's noise thins to ordinary hum — sentries resuming their idle spacing, the treaded unit warming up for its next loop of the same advisory, forty thousand points still counting down toward an expiration nobody collecting them will ever beat. somewhere past the fence line, a ticker updates by one: STOCK LOSS — PREMIUM RESERVE — INVESTIGATION PENDING. it will say the same thing tomorrow.

Far enough now that the cold in the pouch matters more than the drones do. Drops it once to reposition the grip, picks it back up, keeps moving toward wherever tonight's dry corner turns out to be. Personal, tonight was. Personal doesn't mean slower.

the loading dock fades behind into one more set of floodlights among many, its advisory still looping for an audience that's already three blocks gone. the city keeps no separate ledger for one stolen pouch against one old bounty — both just get filed the same way everything here gets filed: pending, unresolved, due to run again tomorrow at the same hour, same crates, same name on the speaker.
